title_orig: Chronica mendosa et ridicula Sarracenorum, de vita Mahumetis et successorum eius
title_es: Crónica falsa y ridícula de los sarracenos, sobre la vida de Mahoma y sus sucesores
title_en: The Faulty and Ridiculous Chronicle of the Saracens, on the Life of Mahumet and his Successors
language: Latin (translation from an Arabic-language Muslim history)
genre: Latin translation of a Muslim historical narrative with Christian marginal notes
edition_original: Printed in Machumetis Saracenorum principis ... ipseque Alcoran, ed. Theodor Bibliander, Basel 1543 (McGill copy on archive.org), chronicle at printed pp. c. 213-236 (Ali's caliphate at p. 220)
licence: archive.org metadata gives no rights or licence field (rights: None); McGill University Library digital copy of a 1543 print
authenticity_note: The Latin is a translation of an unnamed Arabic-language Muslim history; the 1543 print labels it chronica mendosa; the author is anonymous. Date from the Toledan corpus, not re-verified here.
notes: Read on the page image (leaf 241) and on the djvu.txt OCR. Long s printed as f in OCR; the printed form is Ayſca. The same page has a second Aiſca (Aisca uero Ietrib) whose referent is unclear and not used.

title_orig: Ludovici Vivis de Mahomete et Alcorano eius censura, e libris de veritate fidei christianae excerpta
title_es: Censura de Juan Luis Vives sobre Mahoma y el Corán, extraída de su De veritate fidei christianae
title_en: Ludovicus Vives' censure of Mahomet and the Qur'an, excerpted from his De veritate fidei christianae
edition_original: Printed in Machumetis Saracenorum principis ... ipseque Alcoran (Confutationes legis Machumeticae), Basel 1543, section 'De Mahomete et Alcorano ipsius', sub-section on the collection of the Qur'an (page image leaf 277, printed p. 10 of the sub-section)
licence: archive.org metadata gives no rights or licence field (rights: None); McGill University Library digital copy of a 1543 print
authenticity_note: Vives' authorship of the excerpt is given by the print's title; the Aisha statement is reported by Vives from Muslim tradition and he does not name his Arabic source in this passage.
notes: Excerpt inside a volume that also contains Robert of Ketton/Hermann material. Sexually explicit Vives passage naming Aysa is in the same chapter (see excluded.json).
